posts.caption:
Debunked is out now.

Callum Ferris makes his living on a Glasgow podcast, taking apart claims of the paranormal. Then his grandmother, on her deathbed, says something she had no way of knowing.

A psychological thriller with real science in it, and a narrator who copes with almost anything by making a joke of it.

The Noisy Mind is out now, in paperback and Kindle.

For anyone whose mind replays the conversation, rereads the text, and keeps checking long after everyone else has moved on.

The Cable and the Quiet.

Ewan McLeod keeps a GP practice running: the phones, the complaints, the rota, and the store cupboard where a spare network cable sits coiled on the lower shelf. On Thursdays he visits his father, in a house that has been quieter since his mother died. Everyone depends on Ewan. Nobody asks who he depends on.

A novel about grief, about work, and about the people on both sides of the desk. Expected release: Autumn 2027.

slides.text: Almost everyone who lives with anxiety arrives at the same question. It tends to come late, after the thing has happened again, when the worst of it has passed and only the tiredness is left.
If I know my fear isn't rational, why does it still feel so real?
You can know it. The person in the middle of a panic attack often knows, even then, that a racing heart is not a heart attack.
The body answers as though the danger were already in the room. The knowing and the feeling come apart, and you are left somewhere between the two.
Here is the part that changes things. Your brain does not wait for the world and then react to it. It runs slightly ahead, predicting what is about to happen and readying you for it.

posts.caption:
The question almost everyone with anxiety ends up asking, and where the answer starts.

Swipe through the opening of The Calibrated Mind. Out now.

slides.text: The scaffolding on Fotheringay Road had been up for six weeks, and Mara Kerr had learned to read it the way other people read weather. This morning it told her nothing had moved since Friday.

Category B listed, 1887, a tenement that had survived two world wars and a botched harling job in the seventies and was now, apparently, going to be undone by a leaking gutter nobody had looked at since devolution.

She liked the argument of it. The building told you what was wrong with it if you looked properly, and then you told the owners, and the owners argued, and somewhere in the argument was the truth, usually.

posts.caption:
Swipe for the opening of Pentimento, book one of The Provenance Series.

Mara Kerr reads old Glasgow buildings for what they're hiding. She has somewhere to be at half past, and a Thursday she's keeping to herself.

Expected release: Winter 2026.

Rewiring Pain is out now.

How the brain learns pain, and how it can learn safety again. A plain guide to modern pain science for anyone who has lived with pain longer than anyone expected.

This book is not about pretending pain isn't real. It's about understanding what your nervous system has been trying to do.

posts.text: He thought of himself as precise, and precision in the upper sky was a form of power that did not require permission.
posts.caption:
Threnvald, high above the valley of Edrath, in the first pages of The Roots That Breathe.

Book one of The Dimming Canopy, a five-book epic fantasy about power, restraint, and what a bond costs when it's used without asking. Expected release: Summer 2027.

slides.text: There is a particular kind of mind that rarely becomes quiet.
If this describes you, you are not alone. And your mind is not broken.

The same systems that produce the noise also produce sensitivity, depth, and insight. These are qualities the world quietly depends on. The difficulty is not that your mind thinks. The difficulty is that it does not know when to stop.

You do not need a quieter mind.
You need a better relationship with the one you have.

posts.caption:
Swipe through the first page of The Noisy Mind.

For the mind that replays the conversation, rereads the message, and keeps checking long after everyone else has moved on.

Out now in paperback and Kindle.

posts.text: "There's your grandfather," she said. "In his good jumper."
posts.caption:
Six words, an hour before the end. The exact jumper he was buried in, twenty-two years earlier.

Callum has a professional explanation for this. Several, in fact. None of them will stick.

The Calibrated Mind. Retraining anxiety, panic, OCD and trauma-related fear using modern brain science.

You are not broken. You are miscalibrated.

Out now.

posts.text: Ewan had tried throwing it away once. It had reappeared two days later, and since then he had accepted that certain objects in primary care possessed a resilience denied to the people working there.
posts.attribution: The Cable and the Quiet, chapter one
posts.caption:
Anyone who has worked in a GP practice has met this stapler.

The Cable and the Quiet. Expected release: Autumn 2027.

posts.text: A nervous system that has learned pain can also learn safety.
posts.caption:
Pain is real. It's also a protective output of the brain and nervous system, which is why it can carry on after tissues have healed, and why understanding it can change it.

Rewiring Pain. Out now.

posts.label: Pentimento, noun
posts.headline: What shows through.
posts.sub: A pentimento is the trace of an earlier image beneath a painting's surface, where the artist changed their mind and painted over it. Time and thinning paint let the first version back out. The word comes from the Italian for repenting.
posts.caption:
Why the book is called Pentimento.

Dr Alec Muir authenticates paintings for a living. He is very good at finding what lies beneath. The Provenance Series is about people, families and towns that carry earlier versions of themselves just under the surface.

Which word from art or science do you love the sound of?

posts.text: There was a stretch of time when I cried at the wheel on the way to work, three or four mornings a week, for no reason I could point to. Same drive I'd done for years. Nothing had changed except what was running underneath it, and that had become more than I could carry quietly. I assumed for a long time that this was just what a mind did. It isn't.
posts.caption:
Where The Noisy Mind begins.

If your mind rarely goes quiet, you are not alone in it, and none of it means something is wrong with you.

slides.text: I have watched, in a professional capacity, forty-one people greet on cue for strangers pretending to be their dead husbands. I have a spreadsheet. It has colour-coded tabs.

A pal once asked, not unkindly, whether I needed a hobby that didn't involve quantifying other people's grief, and I told her the spreadsheet was the hobby, which she found less reassuring than I'd intended.
None of the forty-one prepared me for my own grandmother.
An hour before the end she opened her eyes, which by then had been shut so long I'd started addressing my remarks to the general vicinity of her face like a man leaving a voicemail.

posts.caption:
Swipe for how Debunked begins.

Callum Ferris debunks psychics for a living. He has a spreadsheet for everything. Then his grandmother says something on her deathbed that no spreadsheet can explain.

Debunked is out now.

posts.label: The Calibrated Mind
posts.headline: The smoke alarm isn't broken.
posts.sub: It goes off when the toast browns because it is doing the one thing alarms do. What has moved is the threshold. Anxiety works the same way: the signals are real, and the point where they get read as an emergency has shifted.
posts.caption:
A thermometer that reads a few degrees high isn't broken. Every part of it works. What has drifted is the relationship between what it reads and what is true.

That's calibration, and it's what The Calibrated Mind is about. Out now.

Inherited. The sequel to Debunked.

Eleven names from a 1950s test cohort. One of them belongs to Callum's own great-uncle. What began as one family's secret has become an app on millions of phones.

Expected release: Spring 2027.

slides.text: If you are reading this, chances are you have lived with pain longer than anyone ever expected, possibly longer than you expected.
You may have tried to be patient. You may have tried to be brave. You may have rested, pushed through, stretched, strengthened, medicated, waited.
Let us start here, clearly and gently: you are not broken. Pain is not a personal failure. It is not weakness. It is not a character flaw.
Pain is a signal, a powerful one. And signals can change.

posts.caption:
Swipe through the first page of Rewiring Pain.

For anyone who has lived with pain longer than anyone expected, and been told everything looks normal.

Out now.

Half past seven in a GP practice before the doors open, and the one man who notices everything that's slightly wrong with it.

Expected release: Autumn 2027.

slides.text: The lights in reception were already on when Ewan arrived, though the practice itself had not yet begun.

He preferred the building at this hour, not because he disliked the staff, or even the patients, though there were individual examples of both about whom he was prepared to remain undecided, but because it was simply easier to understand the place before it filled.
Near the skirting below it, the grey network cable had worked loose from the plastic trunking again.
It wasn't a repair. It was no longer a trip hazard. For the moment those were close enough to the same thing.
slides.attribution: The Cable and the Quiet, chapter one

posts.text: Hope does not mean promising a pain-free life. Hope means restoring choice.
posts.caption:
It means pain no longer runs the conversation.

Rewiring Pain. Out now.

posts.label: Behind the book
posts.headline: The strange science is real.
posts.sub: Princeton ran a lab testing whether minds could nudge machines for nearly thirty years. The Global Consciousness Project has watched random number generators around the world since 1998. The US government paid for remote viewing. Debunked invents the people and the danger. Not the research.
posts.caption:
Everything odd that Callum investigates in Debunked has a real history behind it: the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research lab, the Global Consciousness Project, the remote-viewing programmes, placebo studies and meditation neuroscience.

The question the book asks is simple. What if someone found a way to make money from it?

posts.text: You didn't choose to open this investigation. It opened itself, and now some part of you is standing inside it, going through the evidence.
posts.caption:
Someone pauses half a second too long, or a text comes back shorter than usual.

If you know what happens next in your head, this book was written for you. The Noisy Mind. Out now.

The Roots That Breathe. Book one of The Dimming Canopy.

In Thessaria the ground has started to go wrong. The fortress of Vaelmoor holds its border with dragon fire, the wandering Telaru listen to the roots, and between them stand the dragon Threnvald and the man bound to him.

Expected release: Summer 2027.

posts.text: Anxiety is not a failure of logic. It is what happens when the predictions have been tuned toward danger. And a system that has been tuned can be tuned again.
posts.caption:
Panic, OCD, generalised anxiety and trauma look different on the surface. The Calibrated Mind shows the one machine running underneath all of them, and how it changes.

Out now.

The Deep That Listens. Book two of The Dimming Canopy.

The ground beneath Thessaria has begun to stir. Root-Fathers are dying, a listening post has gone silent, and something far older than the war has started to pay attention.

Expected release: Winter 2027.

posts.label: Rewiring Pain
posts.headline: Pain grows louder in a body that does not feel safe.
posts.sub: A nervous system that feels threatened tightens muscles, sharpens attention and heightens sensation. That isn't imagined. It is physiology, and safety can be learned.
posts.caption:
Why fear and pain feed each other, and why the way out is gradual, patient and possible.

Rewiring Pain. Out now.

slides.text: Threnvald circled where the air thinned into a cold so clean it felt like a blade drawn along the tongue.

The valley of Edrath lay open beneath him, arranged into greens and browns and river-silver, a place that could almost pass for peaceful when he was still high enough to forget what waited beneath it.
He did not think of himself as beautiful, because beauty was a human way of judging things, and humans judged things so they could decide what to claim.
He inhaled deeply and iron entered his mouth.

posts.caption:

A dragon, a valley, and the moment before everything changes.

Expected release: Summer 2027.

posts.text: After she died, there had been people everywhere and yet the place had somehow felt quieter even when it was full.
posts.caption:
A house after a death, full of people and somehow quieter.

The Cable and the Quiet is a novel about grief, and about work, and about what happens when there's no room left between them. Expected release: Autumn 2027.

Pentimento. Book one of The Provenance Series.

When a conservation officer is found dead in her Glasgow flat, DI Ellen Docherty starts asking careful questions. They lead back to Paisley, to a family house full of altered photographs, and to a man who has done this before.

The past doesn't stay buried. It shows through. Expected release: Winter 2026.

A lone Listener, a remote post, a goat, and a ground that has never once surprised her.

Expected release: Winter 2027.

slides.text: Dovra woke before the birds did, which was the only way to wake at the Farrow Post if she wanted the ground quiet enough to hear anything in it.
Three rotations at Farrow, and the ground had never once surprised her.

A goat, currently regarding her with the flat contempt goats reserved for anyone who had not yet fed them.
Dovra fed the goat.

By evening she had eaten, banked the fire, and settled with her ledger to copy the day's marks into the fair record she would carry back at the end of the rotation, a chore she found close to meditative by now, the neat repetition of it, line after line of the ground saying nothing had changed.
She was two lines into it when the ground said something had changed.

posts.text: Somewhere beneath the waiting, for the first time, the ground had begun to listen back.
posts.caption:
The Telaru don't fight with fire. They listen to the roots.

The Roots That Breathe, book one of The Dimming Canopy. Expected release: Summer 2027.

posts.text: Eleven months later, not one of those words has agreed to stick to my grandfather's jumper. They just sort of slide off it and sit there, looking at me.
posts.caption:
Confabulation. Terminal lucidity. Callum has used these words with real confidence on television.

Then he needed them for himself.

slides.text: I was recognised, three times last month, in circumstances distinctive enough that I have started, against my own better instincts, cataloguing them the way I once catalogued mediums.

A woman at a petrol station outside Perth, filling her tank at the pump beside mine, who simply said, "You're the biscuit man," with such complete confidence that I did not have the heart to correct either the nickname or its source.

A teenager on the Glasgow Subway who filmed me for eleven seconds without asking, uploaded it with the caption "the guy from the psychic murder podcast," and generated, by his own later, cheerfully unrepentant account, forty thousand views by lunchtime.

posts.caption:
Eighteen months after Debunked, Callum Ferris is a little bit famous, and not enjoying it.

Swipe for three sightings. Inherited, the sequel to Debunked, has an expected release of Spring 2027.

posts.text: Sometimes the surface is just the surface. Sometimes there's nothing hidden underneath it at all, and looking harder just means you're the one putting something there that was never actually part of the object.
posts.caption:
Leanne Boyd restores paper and photographs. She says this to Alec Muir, a man who believes patience always reveals the truth.

Pentimento. Expected release: Winter 2026.
